# TrustyCard

`Layout` · composition depth: `base`

A static surface that groups related content under a heading. It draws the panel — surface, radius, padding, the rhythm between header and body — and nothing else: the card has no behaviour, no state, and no interaction of its own.

Three places to put content:

| Where | What goes there |
| --- | --- |
| `title` / `description` | the heading (an `<h3>`) and one line of prose about the group |
| `actions` slot | controls acting on the whole group, pinned to the end of the header row |
| default slot | the body — form controls, a table, a read-out, whatever the group is |

A titled card names its own `<section>` through `aria-labelledby`, which makes it a region assistive tech can jump to. An untitled one stays an anonymous `<section>` and adds no landmark noise.

The card sizes to its container: give it a width in your layout (a grid column, a flex track) rather than expecting one here.

**Use it when**
- a group of related controls or read-outs needs boxing off under a heading (a parameter block, a settings group, an inspector panel)
- several pieces of content share one header row that carries the actions for all of them

**Don't use it for**
- a group the user can fold away: use TrustyCollapsible, or TrustyAccordion for several of them
- a message about the current screen: use TrustyBanner, or TrustyAlert when the user must respond
- switching between panels of content: use TrustyTabs
- content that floats above the page: use TrustyPopover, TrustyHoverCard, or TrustyDialog
- the label, hint, and error wiring around a single control: that is TrustyFormItem's job, and it belongs *inside* the card's body

```ts
import { TrustyCard } from '@louislp/trusty-ui'
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | — | Heading for the group, rendered as an `<h3>`. Omit it for an untitled surface. |
| `description` | `string` | — | Short prose under the heading, saying what the group holds. |

## Slots

- `actions`
- `default`

## Examples in Storybook

- Default — Heading and description alone — the plainest card there is.
- TitleOnly — No description: the heading sits straight on top of the body.
- WithDescription — Longer prose wraps, and the card grows with it.
- WithActions — The `actions` slot pins controls to the end of the header row.
- ParameterBlock — The card's real job: a parameter block. Grade fields in the body, a toggle group acting on all of them in the header.
- WithFormContent — A whole form group in the body: fields, checkboxes, a labelled radio group. The card supplies only the surface and the rhythm.
- HeaderOnly — Header row and nothing else: a title with the controls that act on whatever it names.
- Untitled — Untitled: just a surface for the body. It stays an anonymous `<section>`, so it adds no landmark.
- IsALabelledRegion — A titled card is a region named by its own heading, and the controls in its header keep their own names and keyboard paths.
- AngryPepper — Every card component ever written owes a debt to the [A11Y Style Guide's card](https://a11y-style-guide.com/style-guide/section-cards.html), whose demo has been fronted by a furious halved bell pepper since roughly the dawn of time. Ours is an Iconify glyph rather than a photograph, since `TrustyIcon` takes any `collection:icon` name.  Beyond the joke it shows a media card: a thumbnail band in the body, badges under it, and the whole thing still one titled region.
